purpose: Answer-matching rules, shared by the Swift and Kotlin clients. Both test suites read this file, so a rule that drifts on one side fails a test rather than quietly making one player wrong more often than the other (ADR-035).
why_this_matters_more_than_the_wire_form: A move that fails to decode is visibly broken. A rule that accepts 'cafe' for 'café' on one phone and rejects it on the other is a game where one player is simply wrong more often, with nothing on screen to explain why.

normalize.why: Accents fold; the player may not have the key.
Spaces are not part of knowing the answer.
Curly apostrophe, U+2019 — a different character the keyboard may substitute.
Backtick is a modifier symbol, not punctuation, so it has to be listed explicitly on both sides.
A mark that only exists decomposed in NFKD.
Empty stays empty rather than throwing.

matches.why: Any accepted spelling, not only the first.
A different word. Folding must not reach this far.
Empty never matches, even against a non-empty answer.
Whitespace normalises to empty, and empty never matches.
Both sides normalise to empty; still no match, because the guard is on the input being empty.
No accepted answers means no match rather than an error.

nearMiss.why: One deletion, and long enough to be a typo rather than a different word.
One edit, but under the four-character floor: below it, one edit is the difference between most short words.
An exact match is not a near miss; distance is zero, and the rule asks for exactly one.
Length difference over one, rejected before the distance is computed.
Normalises to an exact match, so distance is zero rather than one.
